items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Billy Marrero was over there, with him for a while, and John Lindsay. Well, they'd come over to play in my place

ctx.x: So, Quank would play with us all the week, now, then he played on a Sunday, because we were waiting this week, on a Sunday, he played with, with the Olympic band, but our record drummer was working in the Jewish store, when he played with us on Sundays, on a record drummer, see? Now, Henry Martin played with the Olympic band through the week, with all the outside jobs, Quank played them, see? And we were waiting, see, like, I feel like I want to, you feel like you want to change. I'd slip off and go on over to…
Where did they have those quadrilles, in the other halls, like at Conor Manion?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I used to play in John Lindsay's plays sometimes

ctx.x: It was around 1997 and 1999 when my brother bought that big bass for me. Uh-huh. He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, yes. Roy Palmer was our guitar player. You had to see what became a trombone player? No, let me see what Roy was playing. Roy was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And Joe Johnson was our guitar player. So Joe Johnson learned trumpet and Roy Palmer and Roy Palmer was good too. Joe died. That's what I tell the guys, they read about…
Sure. Why would you play? Bass drum?
